subject.title: [Feature]: Support Slack Enterprise Grid org installs

question: Should OpenClaw accept an opt-in Slack Enterprise Grid org-install mode via https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102372 now, or keep the current per-workspace Slack account model until a different OAuth/persistence design is chosen?
rationale: The request adds new Slack account config and changes workspace authorization and message-delivery boundaries, and the issue already carries a protected `maintainer` label plus security-review labels, so automation should not decide the product/security tradeoff.

options.title: Review linked PR as candidate
options.body: Use the open PR as the implementation path, requiring maintainer review of config compatibility, event-scoped clients, workspace-qualified state, fail-closed delivery, and live org-install proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to per-workspace accounts
options.body: Keep the current single-workspace account model while maintainers design a broader OAuth or installation-store path for multi-workspace Slack usage.

options.title: Reject org-install support for now
options.body: Close the direction only if maintainers decide Enterprise Grid org installs are outside the bundled Slack plugin's supported scope.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as candidate
recommendation.body: Use the open PR as the implementation path, requiring maintainer review of config compatibility, event-scoped clients, workspace-qualified state, fail-closed delivery, and live org-install proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has recent merged Slack config and authorization-surface history, which is the most relevant ownership signal for the product/security choice.
